newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan bar hostess nabbed after 15 years on the run.
newsitem.headline: Japan bar hostess nabbed after 15 years on the run.

text.p: Japanese police have arrested a former bar hostess suspected of killing a colleague, just three weeks before a 15-year statute of limitations was to expire, officials said on Wednesday.
Fukui prefectural police in western Japan arrested late on Tuesday Kazuko Fukuda, 49, who was suspected of strangling to death her colleague in August 1982 on Japan's southern island of Shikoku.
Fukuda underwent plastic surgery several times to disguise herself and assumed various false names during her 15 years on the run, police said.
The statute of limitations for murder was set to expire on August 19.

"I reported Fukuda's arrest to the family of the victim. Our persistent investigation finally bore fruit," Ehime prefectural police officer Kunihiko Nakai, who had been chasing the suspect for nearly 15 years, told a news conference.
In an unprecedented move, the Ehime prefectural police association offered a cash award last August of one million yen ($8,400) for information on the whereabouts of Fukuda.

A major cosmetic surgery hospital in Tokyo, Jujin Hospital, also offered a cash award of four million yen ($33,800) saying it felt a "moral responsibility" for operating on Fukuda, not knowing she was a murder suspect.
Nearly 3,900 tips came in from the public after police and the hospital announced the cash prizes, police said.
Investigators found Fukuda on Tuesday after a man called to say he met a woman resembling Fukuda at a restaurant he frequented.
Fukuda initially denied her identity, claiming she was "Yukiko Nakamura," but gave in after fingerprints matched those of the suspect, officials said.
Both Ehime police and the hospital said they intend to offer the cash prize to the man, Japanese media reported. ($1=118 yen)
